response.sql:
WITH group_avgs AS (
  SELECT e.ordersmark, o.orderflow, AVG(e.fillcount) AS avg_fill
  FROM orderexecutions e
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark
  WHERE e.expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496'
    AND e.expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'
  GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.orderflow
)
SELECT AVG(avg_fill) AS avg_of_group_avgs
FROM group_avgs;

assumptions.assumption: expirespot is compared as text, as the request specifies, so the bounds are lexicographic string comparisons. The schema declares expirespot as text(6) but the documentation says TIMESTAMP, so text comparison may not match true time order for values with differing precision.
orderflow comes from the matching orders row, joined on recordvault = ordersmark. Because recordvault is unique, each execution maps to exactly one order status.
Executions with a NULL orderflow form their own group, since GROUP BY keeps NULL keys. Their group average is still included in the final average unless it is NULL.
AVG ignores NULL fillcount values within each group. A group whose fillcount values are all NULL yields a NULL average, which the outer AVG then ignores.
